answer.question: What should I consider when planning artificial turf in Centennial?
answer.answer: Start with how you want to use the yard, then consider access, shade and existing drainage. Show us the area that is difficult to use now and the landscape you want to retain. If water cost is part of the decision, use the provider and usage on your own bill.

blocks.h2: Show us the space that is difficult to use now.
paras: It may be a worn path from the patio, a shaded patch or the area you would like to turn into a putting green. Point out the problem and the parts of the yard you want to keep. A useful layout leaves room for walking, seating, planting and access as well as turf.
Show us downspouts, low spots and existing drainage routes. Include any proposed fence or gate changes in the discussion. The estimate should make the proposed preparation and drainage work clear.

blocks.h2: Use the provider on your bill.
paras: Centennial addresses are served by different water providers. Centennial Water and Sanitation District serves Highlands Ranch, so its similar name should not be used to assume an offer or rule applies to your City of Centennial address.

Check program eligibility directly before using a rebate in your budget. A turf area no longer needs routine irrigation for living grass, but it still needs cleaning and care, particularly with pets. Compare the change against your own use.

blocks.h2: Use the name on the bill when comparing water costs.
paras: Centennial is served by separate water providers, including Arapahoe County Water and Wastewater Authority. Check the company or district on your bill before applying a watering schedule or rebate to the property.

The similar name can be confusing: Centennial Water and Sanitation District serves Highlands Ranch. Its program should not be assumed to cover a City of Centennial address. Ask your provider whether a proposed landscape change qualifies before including an incentive in your budget.

Artificial turf removes routine irrigation for living grass from the converted area. Allow for the water and time used to clean the surface, particularly with pets, and compare the change using your own bills and planned use.

faq.q: What should I bring if my property has an HOA?
faq.a: Bring the current requirements covering the proposed landscape change and any written response to your layout. Association requirements should be considered alongside the applicable public requirements before installation.
